Featured work

Three builds from the current role at UnitedHealth Group. The first two are LLM agents used by platform engineers; the third is the automation layer underneath them. Internal systems, so the detail here is the shape of the work rather than screenshots.

LLM agent · Incident diagnosis

Teams Issue-Diagnosis Agent

When a service misbehaves, the first questions are always the same, and the answers live in five different tools. This agent meets engineers where the conversation already happens, inside Microsoft Teams, and does the gathering for them.

An engineer describes the issue in plain language. The agent pulls the platform context around that service, works through the likely causes, and hands back a diagnosis with concrete next steps, instead of a blank search box and a pile of dashboards.

Ask in Teams

The engineer posts the symptom in Microsoft Teams, in plain language, with the service name. No new tool to learn, no ticket form to fill in first.

LLM agentsMicrosoft TeamsPythonPlatform APIsObservability signals
LLM agent · Developer experience

Platform Knowledge Assistant

Platform teams answer the same questions every week: how a service gets onboarded, where a runbook lives, what a pipeline stage is waiting on. The answers exist, scattered across internal documentation, runbooks, and portal pages.

The knowledge assistant answers platform questions directly from that internal material, so engineers get the procedure, the link, and the context in one reply instead of interrupting a platform engineer or digging through search results.

  • Grounded in internal sources: answers drawn from platform documentation and runbooks, not model guesswork
  • Built for repeat questions: onboarding, service lifecycle, and how-to questions the team fields daily
  • Part of the platform, not a side demo: maintained alongside the internal developer platform it explains

Automation · Kubernetes platform

Kubernetes Automation and Platform APIs

Running hundreds of microservices by hand means the same operational tasks repeated daily: provisioning, lifecycle changes, routine cluster operations. Each one is a chance for drift and a slow, manual queue for product teams.

Internal platform APIs, written in Go and Python, turned those recurring Kubernetes operations and service lifecycle tasks into self-service automation that teams call directly.

  • API-first operations: Kubernetes operations and service lifecycle management exposed as internal platform APIs
  • Go and Python automation: the tooling layer platform and product teams build on
  • Production support: deployments, CI/CD, and troubleshooting for Java applications, including Spring Boot microservices on Kubernetes

More platform work

The surrounding systems at UnitedHealth Group that the agents and automation sit on top of.

Internal Developer Platform Portal

UNITEDHEALTH GROUP

Built the UI for an internal platform tool that brings everything about a service into one place: the security portal, the GitHub repository list for each service, a vulnerability dashboard, and the application and platform information engineers otherwise hunt across tools.

One portal per service means one starting point for ownership, security posture, and platform status.

Event-Driven ETL for the Developer Dashboard

UNITEDHEALTH GROUP

An event-driven pipeline in Python and Go that consumes GitHub repository creation and application deployment events, transforms the operational metadata, and loads it into PostgreSQL.

The pipeline powers the internal developer dashboard, keeping service and deployment data current as events happen rather than by manual inventory.

CI/CD Standardisation and Dynatrace Migration

UNITEDHEALTH GROUP

Standardised CI/CD across services and migrated observability to Dynatrace SaaS across 100+ services, work recognised in LinkedIn recommendations from the Principal Engineer and Director on the team.

Also part of the platform-wide remit: SLOs and SLIs, error budgets, operational readiness reviews, release quality gates, and 24/7 on-call for the platform.
